skill.name: skill-creator
skill.description: Create, improve, evaluate, benchmark, and package AI skills. Use it to draft instructions, test realistic prompts, compare baselines, and optimize skill triggering.
skill.summary: Create and improve AI skills through structured drafting, evaluation, benchmarking, feedback, and packaging.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown, CSS, JavaScript literals, loopback requests, and harmless identifier names. Confirmed risks include browser injection, inherited secrets in nested Claude calls, symlink packaging, predictable temporary paths, and termination of unrelated port owners. These issues require remediation before publication.

remediation.issue: Generated review pages allow script-context and HTML injection.
remediation.suggestion: Store embedded data in a non-executable JSON element, escape closing script sequences, and render dynamic values with textContent or a trusted sanitizer.

remediation.issue: Nested Claude optimization processes untrusted skill content with broad environment access.
remediation.suggestion: Disable child tools, pass a minimal environment allowlist, isolate the process, and validate the returned description before applying it.

remediation.issue: The review launcher terminates any process already using the selected port.
remediation.suggestion: Do not kill port owners. Bind an available ephemeral port or stop with a clear message that lets the user choose another port.

remediation.issue: The packager follows symlinks and can include files outside the skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Reject symlinks and require every resolved file path to remain inside the resolved skill root before archiving.

remediation.issue: Skill names and shared temporary paths are used without secure path construction.
remediation.suggestion: Validate names with the existing kebab-case rules and use secure temporary files or directories with restrictive permissions.

remediation.issue: Generated pages load fonts and executable spreadsheet code from external services.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor required assets locally or clearly disclose the network dependency and provide an offline mode.

semantic_findings.title: Script-Breakout XSS in Generated Review Viewer
semantic_findings.description: Raw JSON is inserted inside an executable script element. An evaluation string containing a closing script tag can execute JavaScript and expose embedded outputs or feedback.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: json.dumps does not escape a closing script tag for HTML context, and the result is inserted directly into executable script source.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Placeholder Injection in Eval Review Template
semantic_findings.description: The workflow replaces skill and evaluation placeholders without requiring HTML or script-context escaping. A crafted name, description, or query can inject markup or JavaScript.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template contains a raw JavaScript placeholder, and the instructions explicitly require direct replacement without an escaping step.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Through Nested Claude Optimization
semantic_findings.description: Untrusted target skill content is embedded in a nested Claude prompt and executed through the CLI without disabling tools. Injected instructions can redirect the child process.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The complete SKILL.md is interpolated into the prompt, and the child Claude process receives the session environment with no visible tool restriction.

semantic_findings.title: Symlink Following Can Package External Files
semantic_findings.description: The packager follows file symlinks during recursive collection. A crafted skill can include a symlink to an external file and copy its contents into the distributable archive.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Path.is_file and zipfile.write follow file symlinks, while the code performs no symlink rejection or resolved-path containment check.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Skill Name Controls Command-File Path
semantic_findings.description: The trigger evaluator places the target skill name into a filesystem path before validation. Absolute or traversal names can create and delete temporary Markdown files outside the command directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The parsed name is concatenated into command_file, and run_eval does not call quick_validate before writing or unlinking that path.

content.value_statement: Building reliable AI skills requires clear instructions, realistic evaluations, and measured iteration. This skill guides creation, testing, comparison, description optimization, and packaging.
actual_capabilities: Drafts new SKILL.md instructions from user goals, trigger contexts, inputs, outputs, and success criteria.
Reviews existing skills and proposes focused changes while preserving established names and structures.
Creates realistic positive and near-miss negative evaluation prompts with measurable expectations.
Organizes skill and baseline runs for qualitative review and quantitative comparison.
Aggregates pass rates, timing, token usage, variance, and per-assertion results into benchmark reports.
Optimizes skill descriptions through the Claude CLI and packages validated skill directories.
limitations: Description optimization requires the Claude CLI and an authenticated Claude Code session.
Benchmark quality depends on representative prompts, reliable assertions, and sufficient repeated runs.
Browser review pages process local evaluation content and should not be opened before security fixes.
Packaging validates basic structure but does not prove that bundled scripts are secure.

use_cases.title: Draft a New Skill
use_cases.description: Turn a repeatable workflow into a structured skill with clear triggers, instructions, resources, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Improve Team Automation
use_cases.description: Compare an existing skill against a baseline, review failures, and refine instructions using measured results.

use_cases.title: Assess Marketplace Quality
use_cases.description: Build repeatable evaluations, inspect output quality, and document performance before distributing a skill.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill for [task]. Ask about users, trigger phrases, required inputs, outputs, tools, and success criteria before drafting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting from an idea or repeatable workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the skill at [path]. Preserve its name, identify unclear instructions, propose focused edits, and ask whether I want evaluation tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a skill exists but needs clearer or more reliable behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evaluation Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create realistic positive and near-miss negative prompts for [skill]. Define measurable success checks and present the evaluation set for review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when testing trigger accuracy and output quality.

prompt_templates.title: Benchmark and Optimize
prompt_templates.prompt: Benchmark [skill path] against its baseline across [test set]. Analyze variance, collect human feedback, improve the skill, and package the best version.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a rigorous multi-iteration comparison before release.

output_examples.input: Create a skill that standardizes weekly incident summaries.
output: A structured skill draft with trigger guidance and a repeatable reporting workflow.
Three realistic evaluation prompts covering normal, incomplete, and conflicting incident data.
A short validation checklist for required sections and factual support.

output_examples.input: Improve this data-cleaning skill and show whether the revision performs better.
output: A focused revision preserving the skill name and established resources.
Baseline and revised evaluation results with pass rates, timing, and variance.
Human review notes explaining which changes improved outcomes.

output_examples.input: Optimize the description so this skill triggers for relevant requests.
output_examples.output: A concise revised description, train and holdout scores, and a summary of remaining false triggers.

best_practices: Define the user intent, trigger conditions, expected outputs, and dependencies before writing instructions.
Use realistic positive and near-miss negative prompts, then review both measured results and actual outputs.
Preserve the original skill name and compare each revision against a stable baseline.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize against a few narrow prompts without a held-out test set.
Do not accept passing assertions that only check filenames or superficial text presence.
Do not package or publish a skill before reviewing bundled scripts, dependencies, and generated artifacts.

faq.question: Can this skill create a new skill from an idea?
faq.answer: Yes. It gathers requirements, drafts the skill, creates test prompts, and supports review and iteration.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It preserves the skill name, evaluates current behavior, applies focused changes, and compares revisions.

faq.question: Does it test whether a skill triggers correctly?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports positive and negative trigger prompts, repeated runs, thresholds, and held-out testing.

faq.question: Does description optimization require external software?
faq.answer: Yes. The automated optimizer requires the Claude CLI and an authenticated Claude Code session.

faq.question: Can it package the finished skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It validates the basic skill structure and creates a distributable .skill archive.

faq.question: Does a successful benchmark guarantee security?
faq.answer: No. Benchmarks measure selected behavior. A separate security review is required for scripts, dependencies, and data handling.
